content.text: Why this enum covers macOS types too

inlineContent.text: enum across all platforms — the iPhoneOS XCTest header contains every case (rawValues 0…82) including the macOS-only ones (

, etc.). There is no separate iOS-only or iPadOS-only enum: Apple reuses the same numeric value for the same conceptual element across platforms, and just doesn’t emit the macOS-specific cases when scanning iOS apps. Verified against Xcode 16’s iPhoneOS XCTest header at
succeeds for any rawValue Apple currently has in production, which prevents
views for which Apple has a real type.
Cases without a trailing comment are available on iOS (and typically iPadOS / macOS too). A case is only annotated when it does
appear on iOS — either iPadOS-only or macOS-only. Our rules’ applicability checks don’t reference macOS-only types, so cases marked
will never end up in results from an iOS scan.

annotations describe Apple’s emission behavior at time of writing — they are documentation, not compile-time guarantees. If Apple changes which types are emitted on which platforms in a future SDK, the annotations may drift; re-check against
If Apple ever extends the enum past 82, the fallback path in
and log it at debug level — same behavior we’ve always had for
